card.description:
At Gilead, we’re creating a healthier world for all people. For more than 35 years, we’ve tackled diseases such as HIV, viral hepatitis, COVID-19 and cancer – working relentlessly to develop therapies that help improve lives and to ensure access to these therapies across the globe. We continue to fight against the world’s biggest health challenges, and our mission requires collaboration, determination and a relentless drive to make a difference.
 
 Every member of Gilead’s team plays a critical role in the discovery and development of life-changing scientific innovations. Our employees are our greatest asset as we work to achieve our bold ambitions, and we’re looking for the next wave of passionate and ambitious people ready to make a direct impact.
 
 We believe every employee deserves a great leader. People Leaders are the cornerstone to the employee experience at Gilead and Kite. As a people leader now or in the future, you are the key driver in evolving our culture and creating an environment where every employee feels included, developed and empowered to fulfil their aspirations. Join Gilead and help create possible, together.

 Job Description 
 
 Job Description 
 The Director, Quality Risk Management (QRM) is an enterprise Quality leader responsible for defining, governing, and advancing the global strategy for Quality Risk Management across the organization. This role actively supports the Executive Director of Risk and Proactive Quality and has direct leadership accountability for the Quality Risk Management process across PDM.
 This leader provides strategic direction and oversight to ensure that QRM principles, risk‑based thinking and proactive quality approaches are deeply embedded across the Pharmaceutical Quality System (PQS) and operations. The role is accountable for designing, implementing, and sustaining compliant, scalable, and efficient global processes that enable early risk identification, effective risk mitigation, and continuous improvement aligned with cGMP, ICH, and evolving global regulatory expectations.
 As a member of the Extended Central Quality leadership team, the Director drives cultural transformation toward a systemic, proactive, and learning‑oriented quality organization, enabling robust decision‑making, operational excellence, and sustained regulatory compliance across a complex, multinational environment.

 Key Accountabilities 
 Global Business Process Responsibilities and Governance 
 •  Define and execute the global Quality Risk Management framework, with enterprise accountability for strategy, standards, performance, and continuous improvement, enabling early risk identification, mitigation, and prevention across operations and the supply chain.
 •  Design, own, and approve global standards, policies, procedures and training ensuring alignment with cGMP, ICH, and applicable regulatory expectations across all markets.
 •  Drive the evolution of organizational risk maturity, capability, and culture, embedding proactive approach to risk and risk‑based thinking into decision‑making at all levels and across GxP processes.
 • Drive, implement and monitor QRM Master Plans and living Risk Assessment Portfolios across PDM.
 • Ensure effective integration and alignment of Risk and Change Management processes across the PQS and related business processes.  
 •  Ensure effective integration of Proactive HOP process and human‑centric risk mitigation approaches into quality and operational processes.
 •  Collaborate with the Medical Device and Combination Product (MDCP) team to support alignment and harmonization of the QRM and MDCP risk management frameworks, where applicable.
 •  Oversee the enterprise Quality Risk Register and development of the Operations Quality risk profile for senior leadership and management review forums.
 •  Ensure strong linkage and clear requirements between Quality Risk Management and broader enterprise and operational risk management frameworks.
 • Serve as the Module Business Process Lead for the electronic QRM system (e.g., GVault Risk Module), with accountability for maintaining and enhancing its use across QRM activities.
 •  Ensure strong cross‑functional collaboration with Technical, Regulatory, Safety, and Operations partners to manage product, process, vendor and systems risks within GxP.
 • Lead and actively contribute to QRM-related projects and initiatives, including process and system enhancements and continuous improvement opportunities.
 •  Define, implement and monitor metrics, KPIs and dashboards to assess the health and effectiveness of the QRM process.
 • Partner with executive leadership, site heads and functional leaders to align QRM priorities with business objectives
    
 Leadership, Influence, and Stakeholder Engagement 
  
 •  Develop and lead a global network of Risk Leads, Risk Facilitators, Subject Matter Experts, and risk practitioners through direct, matrix, and influence‑based leadership.
 •  Serve as a senior Quality representative in global governance forums, inspections, and regulatory interactions related to Quality Risk Management.
 •  Actively monitor internal and external signals, including audit outcomes, inspection findings, deviations, complaints, and emerging regulatory trends, to inform strategy and priorities.
 •  Sponsor and lead transformational initiatives that leverage QRM and Lean principles, digital enablement, and innovative practices to improve process effectiveness and efficiency.

 Typical People Management Responsibility 

 •  Senior leader of expert teams
 •  Direct and indirect management of global, cross‑functional teams
 •  Matrix leadership across sites, regions, and functions

 Global Remit 

 •  Enterprise‑wide accountability with responsibility spanning all global markets and operating regions
 •  Regular engagement across multiple countries and cultures


 Education, Qualifications, Skills, and Experience 

 Essential 
 •  BS/BA degree with 12+ years or MS/MA/PhD with 10+ years experience in pharmaceutical quality, manufacturing, or a related scientific discipline
 •  Deep subject matter expertise in Quality Risk Management, with demonstrated success implementing global risk programs
 •  Extensive experience working across multiple areas of Quality within a regulated pharmaceutical environment
 •  Proven ability to engage effectively with stakeholders at all levels globally and lead through influence across complex, matrixed, multinational organizations
 •  Strong strategic thinking, communication, and stakeholder engagement capabilities

 Desirable 
 •  Experience leading large‑scale Quality or Operations transformation initiatives
 •  Expertise in Business Process Management, Lean, Six Sigma, or comparable continuous improvement methodologies
 •  Experience overseeing GxP IT systems and digital enablement of Quality processes
 •  Strong business acumen with the ability to analyze trends, assess risk, and build compelling business cases

 Key Responsibilities 
 QC Strategy & Operations
 Lead and oversee all Quality Control functions at the site, including analytical, microbiology, raw materials, in-process, drug substance, drug product, and stability programs across small molecule and biologics platforms

 Build, develop, and lead a high-performing QC organization with strong engagement and accountability
 Foster a quality culture emphasizing scientific rigor, continuous learning, collaboration, and accountability
 Ensure the organization is equipped to support evolving portfolio needs across small molecule and biologics
 Global Alignment, Lean Labs & Continuous Improvement
 Contribute to and lead QC network harmonization and global initiatives, ensuring alignment with enterprise standards and practices
 Drive adoption of global QC policies, systems, and best practices at the site
 Partner with global QC leadership and cross-site teams to enable standardization and capability building
 
 Lead and embed Lean Laboratory principles to improve workflow efficiency, reduce waste, and enhance throughput
 Establish the strategic direction for QC technology, innovation, digitalization, automation, and continuous improvement
 Partner cross-functionally (Manufacturing, MSAT, QA, Regulatory, Supply Chain) to ensure aligned execution and reliable product supply
 Knowledge:
 Experience providing strategic oversight for commercial manufacturing, PPQ, new product introduction, and method transfers, ensuring robust analytical capabilities across the product lifecycle
 Experience contributing to or leading global QC initiatives, network harmonization, and cross-site collaboration efforts, with an enterprise mindset
 Proven ability to balance technical rigor, compliance, and business needs, ensuring effective and timely decision-making
 Strong people leadership and talent development capabilities, including building high-performing teams, developing future leaders, and strengthening organizational capability
 Excellent cross-functional leadership, communication, and stakeholder engagement skills, with the ability to influence at both site and executive levels
 Required:
 Bachelor’s degree in a scientific discipline and 14+ years of experience in the pharmaceutical or biopharmaceutical industry, with significant leadership experience in Quality Control within a GMP-regulated environment required OR 
 Masters degree in a scientific discipline and 12+ years of experience in the pharmaceutical or biopharmaceutical industry, with significant leadership experience in Quality Control within a GMP-regulated environment required OR 
 PhD in a scientific discipline and 12+ years of experience in the pharmaceutical or biopharmaceutical industry, with significant leadership experience in Quality Control within a GMP-regulated environment required
 Recognized technical leader with deep expertise in analytical sciences and Quality Control across small molecule and biologics, and a demonstrated ability to make sound, science-based decisions in complex and ambiguous situations
 Proven experience building and leading strong, technically capable QC organizations, with a focus on developing scientific depth, critical thinking, and problem-solving capabilities across teams
 Strong knowledge of global GMP regulations, inspection management, and data integrity (ALCOA+), with a proven track record supporting regulatory inspections (FDA, EMA, PMDA)
 Demonstrated ability to drive Lean Laboratory principles and a continuous improvement mindset, including process optimization, digitalization, and automation to enhance lab efficiency and performance
 Preferred:
 MS, PhD (advanced degree) in a scientific discipline preferred

card.description:
Karman Space & Defense is a leader in the rapid design, development, and production of critical, next-generation system solutions that align with the U.S. Department of War and its allies' core mission priorities, and meet the accelerating demand for access to space. Building on nearly 50 years of success, we deliver Payload & Protection Systems, Aero/Hydrodynamic Interstage Systems, and Propulsion & Launch Systems to more than 80 prime contractors supporting over 130 space and defense programs.

The Director of Quality, Defense is responsible for overseeing all quality activities, personnel, systems, and performance associated with Defense programs across multiple Karman Space & Defense operating sites. This role provides strategic and operational leadership to ensure all Defense hardware, assemblies, and services meet or exceed contractual, regulatory, and customer requirements. 
 
This position will manage the Defense Quality Engineering organization, supports execution of Defense programs, and ensures consistent application of quality standards and tools across the sector. This leader works in close partnership with the Enterprise Director of Quality to align each site's AS9100 compliant QMS with the emerging enterprise quality architecture and to transition multiple Defense sites toward a unified enterprise certification. 
 
This role is critical in driving disciplined execution, continuous improvement, product integrity, and customer satisfaction within the Defense market segment.

Reports to Vice President, Defense. Functional Partnership with Enterprise Director of Quality (Karman Space & Defense). 
 
**ESSENTIAL DUTIES AND RESPONSIBILITIES** 

* Lead, develop, and manage the Quality Engineering team supporting all Defense programs and projects.
* Build a culture of accountability, collaboration, proactive risk management, and continuous improvement across Defense Quality functions.
* Serve as the primary Defense quality leader to the VP of Defense and the Defense leadership team.
* Ensure the quality of all Defense hardware, assemblies, engineered systems, and services produced across multiple sites.
* Oversee program quality planning, including inspection strategies, qualification/verification plans, critical characteristics control, product safety considerations, and risk mitigation.
* Review and approve quality requirements for Defense proposals, contracts, and manufacturing plans.
* Drive effective root cause analysis, corrective action, and failure review processes for Defense programs.
* Ensure each Defense site maintains compliance to AS9100, customer requirements, and regulatory obligations.
* Provide direct guidance to site Quality Managers/Quality Engineers on QMS implementation, audit readiness, and procedural improvement.
* Support site internal audits, customer audits, DCMA oversight, and third‑party certification audits.
* Partner with the Enterprise Director of Quality to align Defense site QMS structures, documentation, and practices with the enterprise quality framework.
* Support the long-term strategy to transition multiple Defense AS9100 certificates into a unified enterprise certificate.
* Collaborate closely on enterprise initiatives such as configuration management improvements, risk management systems, document control harmonization, supplier quality strategies, and enterprise metrics.

 
**EDUCATION AND EXPERIENCE** 

* Bachelor's degree in engineering, Quality, Manufacturing, or related technical field preferred
* 10 years of experience in aerospace/defense quality roles preferred.
* Strong working knowledge of AS9100, ISO 9001, and Defense customer quality standards.
* Quality Engineering experience with complex programs including design.

**ITAR REQUIREMENTS**

To conform to U.S. Government export regulations, certain positions may require applicants to be a (i) U.S. citizen or national, (ii) U.S. lawful, permanent resident (aka green card holder), (iii) Refugee under 8 U.S.C. § 1157, or (iv) Asylee under 8 U.S.C. § 1158, or be eligible to obtain the required authorizations from the U.S. Department of State.

**TRAVEL REQUIREMENTS**

Occasional travel 0-10% of the time.

Karman Space and Defense is an Equal Opportunity Employer. All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, sex, national origin, age, disability, protected veteran status, or any other status protected by applicable federal, state, or local law.

card.title: Director of Compliance, Quality & Risk
card.description:
POSITION SUMMARY
 
 
Will provide strategic leadership, direction, and oversight of the Laguna Healthcare Corporation (LHC) Compliance, Quality Risk Programs, encompassing all clinical, administrative, financial, and medical practice plan functions. This position is responsible for designing, implementing, and continuously improving enterprise-wide programs that ensure adherence to all federal, state, tribal, and accreditation standards. Serve as the primary authority on compliance matters, leads risk mitigation efforts, manages investigations, and champions a culture of ethics, accountability, and transparency. The Director collaborates with leadership, providers, and staff to promote a culture of continuous improvement, patient safety, and accountability. They oversee performance improvement initiatives, incident reporting systems, compliance activities, and risk mitigation strategies to enhance patient outcomes and organizational effectiveness. This position also plays a critical role in integrating culturally responsive care into quality frameworks, supporting health equity, and ensuring services reflect the values, traditions, and needs of the Tribal population served.
 
 
ESSENTIAL FUNCTIONS
 
 

* Develop, implement, and oversee LHC’s Compliance, Quality Risk programs, policies, and procedures related to standards of conduct; healthcare laws; billing and reimbursement; fraud, waste, and abuse prevention; privacy and security; quality improvement and other compliance risk areas.
* Lead and facilitate internal committees to drive strategic planning for these programs, setting long- and short-term goals, operational plans, and performance measures.
* Conduct organization-wide quality and risk assessments to identify, prioritize, and mitigate compliance risks and improve overall patient outcomes.
* Monitor compliance with healthcare laws, CMS/OIG regulations, HIPAA/HITECH, and Tribal requirements.
* Oversee sanction screening of employees, contractors, and vendors; ensure organization-wide training on sanction monitoring processes. Ensure credentialing, privileging and provider enrollment program is effective.
* Lead internal audits and compliance reviews to ensure adherence to payer rules, regulatory standards, and organizational policies.
* Develop, in collaboration with the CMO, clinical care guidelines, as well as process and system guidelines.
* Manage confidential reporting channels, including the LHC Compliance Hotline, ensuring proper documentation, investigation, and resolution.
* Conduct or supervise compliance investigations; ensure/coordinate corrective actions with HR, legal counsel, leadership, and managers.
* Serve as the organizational liaison with regulatory agencies during audits, investigations, and compliance inquiries.
* Lead and mentor others in root cause analysis (RCA), healthcare failure mode and effects analysis (FMEA) and hazard vulnerability analysis (HVA) teams. Summarize risk management and patient safety data for appropriate evaluation and risk trend analysis.
* Maintain detailed records of compliance efforts, investigative outcomes, and corrective action plans.
* Provide written and verbal compliance reports to executive management, internal Quality Committee, the Board Compliance Committee and the LHC Board of Directors.
* Develop and administer a robust, organization-wide compliance training and education program in conjunction managers and the HR department.
* Lead communication initiatives to promote compliance awareness, ethical conduct, quality management and transparent reporting.
* Provide ongoing consultation to staff and leadership on regulatory requirements and performance improvement measures.
* Develop and coordinate processes to monitor quality of care. Identify opportunities to improve patient care, treatment and services by assisting to implement standard work.
* Oversee accreditation preparation for review by regulatory agencies including AAAHC and/or Joint Commission, educate, and assist department supervisors to maintain appropriate policies and procedures to fulfill requirements and regulations.
* Develop, monitor, and manage department budget.
* Supervise and direct staff and consultants and ensure adequate systems, training and tools to support program goals achievement, performance management and corrective action.

MINIMUM QUALIFICATIONS
 
 
Five (5) years of progressive experience in healthcare compliance, quality or related healthcare roles. Bachelor Degree in Finance/Accounting, Business, Public or Healthcare Administration or related field of study from an accredited college or university. Master's Degree preferred.
 
 
Certified Professional Compliance Officer (CPCO) preferred, Certified in Healthcare Compliance (CHC), Certified in Healthcare Privacy Compliance (CHPC), or Certified Compliance Ethics Professional (CCEP) or equivalent compliance certification, or eligible for and certification obtained within 12 months as condition of hire. Quality Management certification preferred.
 
 
MANDATORY KNOWLEDGE, SKILLS, ABILITIES and COMPETENCIES with proficiency levels
 
 
Ethical Integrity Professionalism — Advanced
 
 
1. Demonstrates unwavering commitment to confidentiality, transparency, and ethical conduct.
 
 
2. Consistently models organizational values and establishes an ethical compliance culture.
 
 
3. Guides organizational decision-making through an ethics-centered approach.
 
 
Regulatory Compliance Expertise — Advanced
 
 
1. Interprets and applies federal, state, and Tribal healthcare regulations with precision.
 
 
2. Advises leadership on complex regulatory issues and emerging compliance risks.
 
 
3. Ensures organizational alignment with OIG, CMS, HIPAA/HITECH, and other regulatory standards.
 
 
Analytical Critical Thinking — Advanced
 
 
1. Uses advanced analytical methods to identify trends, risks, and system vulnerabilities.
 
 
2. Evaluates complex scenarios, synthesizes large volumes of information, and provides clear recommendations.
 
 
3. Leads continuous improvement initiatives using data-driven insights.
 
 
Investigation Problem-Solving — Advanced
 
 

* Conducts or oversees thorough investigations into compliance concerns.
* Demonstrates strong evidence analysis skills and draws objective, well-supported conclusions.
* Designs and monitors corrective action plans to ensure sustainable resolution

Leadership Influence — Advanced
 
 
1. Leads cross-functional teams and committees with confidence and clarity.
 
 
2. Influences organizational behavior through effective communication, coaching, and ethical leadership.
 
 
3. Builds trust and credibility with executives, clinical leaders, and staff.
 
 
Communication Interpersonal Effectiveness — Advanced
 
 
1. Clearly communicates complex regulatory concepts to varied audiences.
 
 
2. Prepares high-quality written reports and delivers professional presentations.
 
 
3. Maintains strong interpersonal relationships across diverse stakeholder groups.
 
 
Training Education Development — Intermediate to Advanced
 
 
1. Designs tailored compliance training programs for all workforce levels.
 
 
2. Assesses training effectiveness and adjusts content to address knowledge gaps.
 
 
3. Promotes consistent awareness of compliance responsibilities.
 
 
Project Program Management — Intermediate to Advanced
 
 
1. Manages multiple projects simultaneously while meeting deadlines.
 
 
2. Develops strategic and operational plans for the Compliance Program.
 
 
3. Implements structured processes for tracking progress and outcomes.
 
 
Risk Management Continuous Improvement — Advanced
 
 
1. Conducts comprehensive risk assessments and ongoing monitoring activities.

**Ready to make your next big professional move? Join us on our journey to achieve our big dream of building the most loved restaurant brands in the world.**

 

Restaurant Brands International Inc. is one of the world's largest quick service restaurant companies with nearly $49 billion in annual system-wide sales and over 33,000 restaurants in more than 120 countries and territories.

RBI owns four of the world's most prominent and iconic quick service restaurant brands – TIM HORTONS®, BURGER KING®, POPEYES®, and FIREHOUSE SUBS®. These independently operated brands have been serving their respective guests, franchisees and communities for decades. Through its Restaurant Brands for Good framework, RBI is improving sustainable outcomes related to its food, the planet, and people and communities.

RBI is committed to growing the TIM HORTONS®, BURGER KING®, POPEYES® and FIREHOUSE SUBS® brands by leveraging their respective core values, employee and franchisee relationships, and long track records of community support. Each brand benefits from the global scale and shared best practices that come from ownership by Restaurant Brands International Inc.

**Director, Quality Assurance**

*BURGER KING | UNITED STATES & CANADA | MIAMI, FLORIDA*

**Position Overview**

Burger King is seeking an experienced, collaborative and results-oriented Director of Quality Assurance to lead product quality and supplier quality performance across the U.S. and Canadian restaurant system. This leader ensures that products consistently meet approved specifications and guest expectations, while driving measurable improvements in product quality, consistency and supplier performance.

The Director serves as the primary product quality assurance leader and communication point of contact for the Burger King system, including franchisees, and works closely with suppliers and cross-functional partners. This position is not responsible for ownership or management of the Food Safety function. * + Strong Organization Skills

Minimum High School Diploma or GED Required.

Required

card.title: Sr Director, Quality Control - Analytics & Product Testing
card.description:
Advancing medicine to save lives. Together.  
  
 Thanks to many decades of experience and our passion for what we do, we make an essential contribution to the global availability of biopharmaceuticals, especially for patients with rare and serious diseases.  
  
 Rentschler Biopharma SE is a leading contract development and manufacturing organization (CDMO) focused exclusively on client projects. We offer customized full-service solutions for bioprocess development and the production of complex biopharmaceuticals. As a German family-owned company with an international footprint and global reach, we combine experts, expertise and years of experience to develop best-in-class solutions – together with our clients.
 Rentschler Biopharma has approximately 1,400 employees and is headquartered in Laupheim, Germany, with a site in Milford, MA, USA. In 2024, we joined the United Nations Global Compact, underlining our commitment to sustainability.  
  
 As an independent family-owned company, we live by the motto: Many hands, many minds - ONE TEAM! Open, respectful cooperation characterizes our working environment, where quality awareness, diligence and responsibility are our top priorities. With all the diversity of our talents in the Rentschler team, we pursue one vision together: advancing medicine to save lives. 
 
 
 
As a member of the Rentschler Biopharma Quality Control leadership team in Milford, the Sr Director Quality Control - Analytics & Product Testing will primarily be responsible for leading a Quality Control team responsible for analytical method qualification/validation, testing incoming samples (including process intermediates, drug substance and/or drug product), and providing timely results that support GxP manufacturing and product disposition. The QC Analytics & Product Testing team is composed of analytical leaders, scientists and QC analysts that cover 7-day per week testing. This role will collaborate with Quality Control Technical Services and Quality Operations Support & Stability staff to periodically evaluate processes to ensure that QC activities are efficient, timely in terms of delivery of client contract deliverables, and safeguard data integrity. The successful candidate will need to be flexible and agile with the ability to pivot quickly to changing circumstances and business needs.  
  
 Duties and Responsibilities 

 Lead QC Analytics & Product Testing team and laboratory activities
 Hire and develop employees within the department, while setting clear expectations for success
 Provide active feedback, coaching and employee development
 Act as Portfolio manager for QC project work including scheduling, prioritizing and resource planning to ensure client contract deliverables are met
 Oversee analytical method transfer and method validation activities – requiring in-depth understanding of protein chemistry and analytical chemistry methodologies (incl. peptide mapping, glycan analysis, SEC-HPLC, IEX-HPLC, potency analysis by chromogenic assay)
 Participate in Milford Site Quality Leadership team meetings and follow up action plans
 Collaborate within QC to support authoring, review and/or approval of QC related documents ensuring all appropriate documents are generated and retrievable per GMP standards in support of regulatory submissions and inspections
 Support the team in managing OOS/OOT investigations, deviations and change controls, and implementing appropriate CAPA as it relates to QC
 Provides representation in customer and authority audits and implementation of resulting corrective measures
 Responsible for supporting operational aspects of the QC Analytics laboratory, including data verification, PO management, records management, etc.
 Drives continuous improvement initiatives to enhance productivity and efficiency within QC
 Collect and report quality control metrics via Quality Management Reviews and the Quality Council
 Consistently advise site and Quality management of potential and actual actions that could adversely affect the business; represent quality exposures or represent opportunities to be pursued
 Promotes a strong Quality Culture based on the Rentschler core values
  
 Qualifications 

 A bachelor's or master's degree in chemistry, biochemistry or a related life science field with substantial hands-on experience in Quality Control related activities
 18+ years of industry experience in a GMP QC environment, with a minimum of 8+ years of managerial and project management experience
 Leadership skills to manage technical and laboratory personnel 
 Strong sense of accountability, self-motivation, and drive in meeting project objectives
 Direct experience in managing and overseeing QC related activities internally and at third party vendors
 Understanding of FDA/EU/ICH regulations and guidance related to critical quality attributes, release testing, analytical validation and transfer, and stability testing
 Proven ability to lead and implement multiple projects/tasks simultaneously with competing and/or changing priorities ensuring effective time management
 Excellent facilitation and project management skills, with strong verbal and written communication skills
 Ability to effectively communicate across all levels and cross-functional teams
 Ability to work independently as well as collaboratively in a team environment
 
 Working Conditions 

 Normal office working conditions: computer, phone, files, fax, copier
 Personal Protective Equipment must be worn as required
 Minimum travel required
 Will interact with other people
 Pace may be fast and job completion demands may be high 
 
 Working Conditions 


 PPE as required

 ____________________________________________________________________________ Base Pay Range 

 $210,000 - $260,000 

 Disclosure Statement 

 Rentschler Biopharma, Inc is committed to fair and equitable compensation practices. The base pay range listed for this position is the anticipated annual base salary range the organization reasonably, and in good faith, expects to pay for this position at this time. Actual compensation is determined based on several factors that may include seniority, education, training, relevant experience, relevant certifications, geography of work location, job responsibilities, or other application factors permissible by law. The annual base salary is just one component of our Total Rewards package, which also includes our annual discretionary bonus program, medical insurance, our generous 401K program, plus a host of other benefits to aligned to support our employees’ personal and professional wellness. The salary pay range is subject to change and may be modified at any time.

Leads and directs process and overall quality improvement activities that produce better patient care and more efficient operations. Develops programs to review and evaluate patient care and outcomes. Implements a strategy and plans for a quality improvement function within the facility in collaboration with the administrative and clinical leaders of the hospitals that Cohesive manages. Tracks and presents results of improvement efforts and ongoing measures of clinical processes to management. Provides input to strategic decisions that affect the functional area of responsibility. May give input into developing the budget. Capable of resolving escalated issues arising from operations and requiring coordination with other.

 

**POSITION QUALIFICATIONS**

Minimum Qualifications:

* Ability to project a professional Image.

* Knowledge of regulatory standards and compliance requirements.

* Knowledge of techniques and methods of patient care services and instructions for patients and their families.

* Working knowledge and ability to apply professional standards of practice in job situations.

* Strong organizational and analytical skills.

* Persons who have been found guilty by a court of law of abusing, neglecting, or mistreating individuals in a health care related setting are ineligible for employment in this position.

* Freedom from illegal use of drugs.

* Ability to perform each position responsibility satisfactorily with or without reasonable accommodation. Reasonable accommodations may be made to enable individuals with disabilities to perform the essential duties of the position.

* Ability to understand that safety is a condition of employment. Unsafe acts or conditions will be reported to the supervisor

* Must be computer literate with ability to enter information in the EHR system and compile reports or data as requested.

* Must be able to read, write and speak English.

**POSITION DETAILS:**

* Provide leadership in ongoing development and implementation of a data-based monitoring, tracking and process improvement system that will ensure compliance with the state of OK/TN/KS requirements for quality management.

* Ensures review of clinical records regarding diagnosis, treatment and summary of member's progress. Ensures individual and systemic quality of care. Confers with other practitioners and technical experts in own field of specialization, to broaden knowledge, acquire specific information, or obtain advice or consultation.

* Implements process improvement and integrates quality throughout the organization.

* Assures regulatory compliance within assigned areas of responsibilities and in collaboration with peers. Establishes external networks to facilitate benchmarking and practice excellence. Demonstrates leadership within and outside the facility to promote a model of excellence in practice, education, and administration.

* Ensures that review of medical records for quality of care issues, compliance with best practices, and potential litigation concerns occurs as needed.

* Performs other duties as assigned.

 

**Education and/or Experience:**

* Must possess current state RN license and BLS certification.

card.description:
Exciting leadership opportunity with a growing skin care manufacturing company. At Episciences, the Director of Quality and Compliance is responsible for ensuring the marketing compliance of topical skin care products domestically and internationally and has oversight of manufacturing quality assurance and control processes in-house and at third party testing facilities. The ideal candidate will have working knowledge/experience of FDA cosmetic and OTC drug regulations; EU, UK, and Canada cosmetic regulations; and cGMP. The Director of Quality and Compliance routinely monitors current and new regulations to ensure products are compliant within all intended markets.

As the head of the Quality Control and Assurance team, the Director of Quality and Compliance is responsible for the review/approval and maintenance of master product formulae, master labeling copies and maintenance of standard operating procedures. The Director of Quality and Compliance also reviews and trends: customer complaints, raw materials, quality processes and finished product testing for release to Manufacturing,

Ideal Qualifications for this Position:

* Bachelor’s degree in chemistry is preferred

* 5+ years of management experience is preferred

* 5+ years of experience in food, drug and/or cosmetic manufacturing GMPs and Regulatory

* Ability to read and comprehend FDA CFRs as well as other domestic and international Regulatory documentation

* Excellent communication and presentation skills

* Excellent organization, filing and document writing skills

* FDA audit experience is a plus

What to expect as the Director of Quality and Compliance at Episciences Inc.:

* Discounted award-winning Episciences Inc. products

* A Business Casual Company and Culture

* Company paid medical, dental, vision and life insurance coverages

* Company matching retirement plan

* Paid holidays (11 per calendar year)

* Vacation and PTO accrual

card.title: Director, Quality Improvement
card.description:
Shirley Ryan AbilityLab is the global leader in physical medicine and rehabilitation for adults and children with the most severe, complex conditions. By joining our team, you’ll be part of our life-changing mission and vision. You’ll contribute to an innovative, multifaceted culture that is second to none — one that embraces collaboration, excellence, discovery and compassion. You’ll play a role in something that’s never been done before as we integrate science and clinical care to help patients achieve better, faster outcomes — as we Advance Human Ability, together.

**Job Description Summary**

The Director, Quality Improvement provides strategic leadership, oversight, and operational direction for quality improvement, regulatory readiness, accreditation compliance, and performance improvement initiatives across the Shirley Ryan AbilityLab system of care, inclusive of the Alliances. This role partners closely with clinical, operational, and administrative leaders to foster a culture of continuous improvement, patient safety, accountability, and high reliability in alignment with organizational goals and Envision 2030 priorities. 
 
The Director leads enterprise quality improvement initiatives, coordinates accreditation and regulatory readiness activities, advances data-informed decision-making, and supports ongoing compliance with applicable standards and requirements, including CARF, The Joint Commission, CMS, and other regulatory bodies. The Director serves as a key advisor and partner to clinical, operational, and administrative leaders to advance quality outcomes, patient safety, operational effectiveness, and organizational excellence.

**Job Description**

**The Director, Quality Improvement will:**

 

* Provide leadership and direction for quality improvement, performance improvement, accreditation, and regulatory readiness programs across the Shirley Ryan AbilityLab system of care, with initial focus at the flagship hospital
* Develop and lead quality and performance improvement initiatives utilizing evidence-based methodologies and frameworks to advance regulatory compliance, patient outcomes, and operational excellence across the Shirley Ryan AbilityLab system of care, with initial focus at the flagship hospital.
* Partner with leaders to align quality initiatives with strategic organizational priorities and Envision 2030 goals.
* Promote a culture of continuous improvement, transparency, accountability, and interdisciplinary collaboration.
* Oversee the identification, development, tracking, analysis, and reporting of key quality, patient safety, operational, and regulatory performance measures. Identify trends, risks, and opportunities for improvement.
* Collaborate with leaders and teams to identify opportunities for improvement and implement sustainable corrective action plans.
* Lead the annual development, evaluation, and update of the organization's Quality Assurance and Performance Improvement (QAPI) Plan and support ongoing monitoring of organizational performance against established priorities.
* Support departments in developing measurable goals, dashboards, and improvement plans to drive organizational performance.
* Direct organizational accreditation and regulatory readiness efforts, including preparation for CARF, The Joint Commission, CMS, and other applicable surveys and reviews.
* Maintain knowledge of evolving regulatory and accreditation standards and assess and communicate organizational impacts, risks, and recommended actions to leadership.
* Partner with operational and clinical leaders to ensure policies, procedures, workflows, and practices align with regulatory requirements and best practices.
* Oversee regulatory and accreditation survey response activities, corrective action plans, and ongoing monitoring to ensure timely and sustained compliance.
* Oversee the development and presentation of quality and performance reports, dashboards, and executive-level analyses to support organizational decision-making.
* Oversee the development and presentation of quality and performance reports, dashboards, and executive-level analyses that provide meaningful insights, support organizational accountability, and inform leadership decision-making.
* Serve as a subject matter expert and resource for quality improvement, accreditation, regulatory readiness, and performance improvement methodologies.
* Partner with leaders, physicians, clinicians, and operational teams to build organizational capability and accountability for quality, patient safety, and performance improvement.
* Develop and facilitate training, education, and communication strategies related to accreditation standards, regulatory requirements, and quality initiatives.
* Represent Quality and Safety on organizational committees, councils, and interdisciplinary teams as assigned.
* Perform all other duties that may be assigned in the best interest of the Shirley Ryan AbilityLab.

**Reporting Relationships**

* Reports directly to the Executive Director, Quality and Safety.
* Provides leadership and oversight to assigned quality, accreditation, regulatory, and performance improvement staff.

**Knowledge, Skills & Abilities Required**

* Master's degree in healthcare administration, business administration, public health, nursing, allied health or a related healthcare field required.
* Minimum of seven years of progressively responsible experience in healthcare quality improvement, accreditation, regulatory compliance, patient safety, or performance improvement, within a hospital, rehabilitation, or complex healthcare environment. .
* Relevant quality, patient safety, accreditation, or healthcare certification (e.g., CPHQ, CPPS) is required or obtained within two years of hire.
* Comprehensive knowledge of healthcare quality and performance improvement methodologies, accreditation standards, and regulatory requirements, with demonstrated experience leading accreditation and regulatory readiness activities. Knowledge of CARF, The Joint Commission, CMS, and other applicable healthcare regulatory and accreditation requirements.
* Strong analytical and problem-solving skills with demonstrated ability to interpret complex quality, patient safety, operational and regulatory data and translate findings into actionable recommendations.
* Exceptional communication, facilitation, and relationship-building skills, with demonstrated ability to collaborate with and influence physicians, clinical leaders, operational leaders, and other stakeholders across all levels of the organization.
* Demonstrated project and change management capabilities, including the ability to lead complex, cross-functional initiatives from planning thru implementation and sustained adoption.

* Normal office environment with little or no exposure to dust or extreme temperature undefined

card.description:
Job Description 
 GENERAL SUMMARY: 
 The Quality Operations Director provides operational leadership for commercial resupply and lifecycle management of primary and secondary packaging and labeling across a global CMO network. The role translates strategy, capacity plans, and business priorities into an efficient operating model across global CMO portfolios.  
 The Director leads a risk-based quality oversight structure required to assure compliant, reliable, and uninterrupted commercial supply. The role leads a high-performing organization and serves as a senior Quality partner to CMO leadership, Vertex Sr Director of quality operations, Manufacturing &technical operations, Supply Chain, Regulatory, Launch/Technical Quality, and other internal and external stakeholders.
  
 KEY DUTIES AND RESPONSIBILITIES: 
 The responsibilities of this position will include, but are not limited to, the following:
 Lead operational quality oversight for commercial resupply and lifecycle management of finished goods primary and secondary packaging and labeling activities across US and UK/EU CMOs.
 Translate departmental strategy and business priorities into operational quality plans, resource priorities, and execution expectations for the packaging and labeling quality team
 Proactively build team capability, an inclusive environment and drive consistent team execution. Provide direct leadership for people managers and/or senior staff, demonstrating understanding of team strengths and development areas and leveraging expertise effectively through performance management, talent development, coaching, and succession planning.
 Lead prioritization, decision-making, and coordination across packaging and labeling operational quality activities so that issues are managed at the appropriate level and business results are delivered across the organization
 Act as the primary escalation leader for significant packaging and labeling operational quality issues, ensuring timely triage, risk assessment, communication, and appropriate resolution
 Lead cross-functional operational forums related to commercial resupply and lifecycle packaging and labeling quality, ensuring clear accountability, decision tracking, follow-through, and alignment across internal stakeholders and CMO partners
 Ensure robust procedural oversight of exemption management, QP-related activities, artwork and packaging process change controls, and batch documentation review within the scope of the function

card.description:
Job Description 
 General Summary: 
 
 The Sr. Director, GCP Operational Quality will advance and provide strategic direction and oversight of the strategies, mechanisms, processes and capabilities for effective and proactive quality risk management across respective product/therapeutic program area(s) (e.g.; Cystic Fibrosis). This individual will serve as the GCP Operational Quality Lead and have overall responsibility for lifecycle review of risks to quality through ensuring appropriate oversight, mitigation strategies and plans enabling clinical quality outcomes and real time inspection readiness. This individual will provide strategic oversight and leadership for Quality Management Reviews, ensuring transparency for gaining insights regarding effectiveness of risk mitigation strategies/controls, proactive and sustainable clinical quality, and compliance for assigned programs. This individual will integrate end-to-end quality principles and review preparedness at key milestones in alignment with organizational and project milestones. The Sr. Director, GCP Operational Quality will foster strong collaboration and partnership with business stakeholders and will ensure alignment with Quality leadership and teams (e.g. audit, vendor management) in development of integrated strategies for clinical programs, process and vendor oversight, inspection readiness, and assurance. This individual will provide strategic guidance and direction to the integrated benchmarking and external environmental monitoring for identifying emerging industry trends and best practices (e.g. operating models, capabilities) to facilitate maximum value to evaluation of the health of the quality system and identification of cross functional risks that will require assessment by the GXP functional areas. The Sr. Director, GCP Operational Quality will be one who has demonstrated success in engaging clinical/medical teams and cross-functional stakeholders for collaboration in applying quality risk management approaches (e.g. Quality by Design) for inspection readiness, quality outcomes and operational excellence, balancing design of models with practicality of application for effectiveness of outcomes. 
 
 
 Key Duties and Responsibilities: 
 Provides strategic direction and oversight to development, execution and continual improvement of quality risk management/mitigation and inspection readiness strategies across program areas
 Design program-specific Quality strategy and partner with business stakeholders across Global Clinical Operations, Medical Affairs, Regulatory, etc. for alignment of quality strategies, goals and approaches in support of quality outcomes and real time inspection readiness
 Provides strategic leadership to implementation of risk-based approaches to quality for clinical development program(s) – e.g. Quality by Design principles, risk-based quality management (RBQM) and ensure effectiveness of mechanisms for ongoing quality risk monitoring, mitigation and management
 Provides strategic oversight and ensures development, implementation and maintenance of the quality plan(s) summarizing the result of evidence of quality activities
 Leads and/or provides strategic direction/oversight to staff leading quality working groups to define integrated quality plans/activities to deliver the overall quality strategy across QA functions (e.g. audit, operations, vendor management, inspection preparedness and management, etc.)
 Engages and provides consultation to business partners in advancing proactive and leading quality approaches incorporating best practices and establishing/developing strategies for new models, technologies, and practices across clinical development
 Serves as Quality representative to cross-functional clinical development teams, R&D Leadership and quality governance bodies as applicable
 Manages for cause, critical and/or complex quality issues for Strategic leadership of proactive inspection readiness strategies and review at key project milestones in support of organizational deliverables and decision-making models
 Provides strategic direction in the oversight and continual advancement of the GCP QMS framework/model for optimizing operational performance across QA and the business areas as well as in collaboration with the Integrated QMS function in QA
 Leads/chairs integrated GCP QA Operational Management Reviews for ensuring cross-QA transparency and gaining insights regarding efficiency, inspection readiness, and operational performance across QA, including identification of opportunities for improvement
 Partners with QA leadership and managers for determination of needs for tools, metrics, mechanisms and systems enabling individual manager accountability and ownership for decision making in ensuring operational performance (budget, resource, goals/objectives) across their scope of responsibility
 Provides expertise and strategic oversight and direction to development and advancement of progressive models and mechanisms for risk management identification, mitigation and communications across QA supporting enhanced planning, prioritization, resourcing strategies and projection of future needs and capabilities
 Provides leadership coordination and direction to benchmarking with external peers and industry for establishing QA operational performance targets/goals in support of excellence, value and impact
 Provides leadership and partners with QA management in proactive and strategic planning for QA and translation of the strategy to operating plans for execution
 Partners with stakeholders across enabling functions for alignment of strategies, and optimization of programs for delivery, specifically with respect to corporate vs. QA-specific initiatives
 
 Knowledge and Skills: 
 Broad and deep global health regulatory agency knowledge and experience across multiple GCP/PV with current knowledge of industry trends and best practices for efficiency, compliance and effectiveness
 Knowledge and demonstrated experience in application of risk-based quality principles (e.g. QbD) in a pharmaceutical environment
 Broad and deep operational and project management knowledge and experience
 Demonstrated strategic planning and execution skills required
 Proven ability to design/evolve and /or implement quality strategies and operational planning and oversight in a fit-for-purpose manner enabling effectiveness, flexibility and adaptability in a dynamic and evolving business model
 Current knowledge of industry trends and best practices- for progressive quality risk management in a regulated environment
 Developing individuals and teams; proven leadership capabilities within multi-level organization
 Creative, innovative leadership experience complemented with strong change management experience, adaptability, resourcefulness
 Excellent communication skills and a proven track record Influencing/building/promoting a culture of Quality and Excellence
 Operational Excellence experience with proven ability to lead improvement projects-Experience with implementation and execution of program and enterprise risk management, Root Cause Analysis and other Operational Excellence experience, such as LEAN, DMAIC, Six Sigma
 Strong problem solving and critical thinking skills, accompanied by Analytical thinking/Data Analysis skills required to make sound decisions
 
 Education and Experience: 
 M.S. (or equivalent degree) and 10 +years of relevant work experience, or
 B.S. in a scientific or allied health field (or equivalent degree) and 15+ years of relevant work experience, or relevant comparable background
